telegram.title: Telegram
telegram.desc: A short post with a link to the article, posted to your channel via a bot. Not the full article: a 4096-character message cap would break it into walls of text.

site.title: Website
site.desc: Finished articles are published to your site's blog automatically via a secret receiver token.

vk.title: VK
vk.desc: Native community posts built from finished articles — the format adapted for VK.

dzen.title: Dzen
dzen.desc: Dzen pulls new articles from your blog's RSS feed itself. No code needed — connect once.
dzen.s1: Open your Dzen channel settings and verify ownership of ideata.io. The meta tag and verification file are already on the site.
dzen.s2: In the import section paste the RSS feed URL — the Russian one for a Russian-language channel.
dzen.s3: Save. From then on every new article travels to Dzen on its own; the feed carries full texts and covers.
dzen.note: Dzen picks up posts published AFTER the feed is connected. Older archives will not be pulled in — that is their policy, not a feed problem.

threads.title: Threads
threads.desc: An announcement with a link goes to your Threads account. A long title is split into a thread.

x.title: X (Twitter)
x.desc: A thread from the article is posted to your X account. Connect by signing in — no tokens to paste.
x.oauthNote: Threads are posted to your X account. Access renews itself. The right to write comes from your X API tier, not from signing in: a free key returns 403 on publish.

medium.desc: Medium imports a published article by its URL and sets canonical back to the original — better for SEO than publishing via API.
medium.s1: Copy the URL of a published article from your blog.
medium.s2: Open Medium's import page and paste the URL — it pulls the text, images and tables.
medium.s3: Review the draft and publish. Medium sets the canonical to your original automatically.
medium.note: Medium has issued no new API tokens since 2023. Import by URL replaces it and gives a better result: without canonical the copy would compete with your own site in search.

devto.desc: Publishes via an API key together with a canonical to the original. The key comes from your dev.to settings.

bluesky.desc: A thread on Bluesky via app password. Open protocol, no review, no cost.

mastodon.desc: An announcement with a link on your Mastodon account. Any instance — it is a federation.

linkedin.desc: Posts to your LinkedIn feed over OAuth — just sign in. Their API does not publish articles, only posts.

wordpress.desc: Publishing to a WordPress blog: application password for self-hosted, OAuth for WordPress.com.

app.title: Application password
app.desc: For any self-hosted site. Works right away, no plugins and no app registration.

oauth.title: WordPress.com OAuth
oauth.desc: For WordPress.com blogs and self-hosted sites connected through Jetpack — they show up in the same account.

ghost.desc: The full article into your Ghost blog, with a canonical link to the original.

telegraph.desc: The whole article on telegra.ph — a fast page, no signup, no ads.

docs.title: Receiver contract
docs.subtitle: Everything Blog Writer sends to your site — the full contract.
docs.promptHint: You build the receiver on your side: a few routes on your backend. The button above copies a ready-made spec — paste it into Claude Code or Cursor, or hand it to a developer. The base URL and header are already filled in from the fields above; the token never goes into the text.

s1.d: we POST {base}/blog/ingest with a sourceId field. Publishing again reuses the same sourceId, so it is an update, not a second post.

s2.t: The receiver answers id and slug
s2.d: we use them to show a link to the article and to remember it is live. We wait no longer than 15 seconds.

s3.d: we send DELETE {base}/blog/ingest?sourceId=… A 404 reads as “already gone” and counts as success.

docs.requiredNote: * — required field. Empty values are never sent.
docs.curlHint: The same request we make. Put your token in the BLOG_INGEST_TOKEN environment variable.
docs.timeoutNote: Our timeout is 15 seconds: move heavy work (re-uploading the cover, rebuilding a static site) to the background and answer right away. Drafts (status: draft) must not be publicly reachable — not in listings, not by direct link.

flow.auto: No separate step: the article goes here on its own when you press Publish in the article. Per-channel results are shown right there.
flow.x: The thread is built in the article, under Social, and goes to X with the Publish button.
flow.threads: An announcement with a link is sent on its own when you press Publish in the article.

linkedin.note: Posts go to your LinkedIn feed. Their API does not publish articles — posts only. Access renews itself; if it is revoked, the channel will ask you to reconnect.
linkedin.revokeNote: The app secret stays on the server — we only store the account token. You can revoke access here or under LinkedIn “Permitted services”.

x.oauthNote: Threads are posted to your X account. Access renews itself. The right to write comes from your X API tier, not from signing in: a free key returns 403 on publish.
x.revokeNote: The app secret stays on the server — we only store the account token. You can revoke access here or under X “Connected apps”.
